Subject: Redwood trial — procurement & billing next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier, Jenny — really helpful to align on your trial goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on procurement and the commercial path.

Recap from today's discovery:
- Trial scope: 2-week sandbox for the recommendation engine + embeddings for search (~100k queries/day target)
- Success criteria: 95th pct latency < 500ms, inference cost target <$0.002 per recommendation, and integrated embeddings into search ranking with comparable relevance lift to your current prod baseline
- Stakeholders: Jenny (Product), Kyle (Procurement) — procurement will own PO/invoice path

Open procurement/commercial questions for you to confirm:
1) Procurement path: do you plan to purchase via PO (vendor invoice) or do you prefer Redwood on AWS Marketplace (consolidated marketplace billing)?
2) Billing start: do you prefer billing to start immediately when the trial begins, at the trial end, or when you hit the agreed conversion threshold? We typically support: immediate billing, billing-on-conversion (when threshold met), or billing after trial end.
3) Payment terms: are Net 30 and a PO number required on invoice? Any special vendor form or W-9 needed?

Proposed next steps:
- Please confirm procurement preference (PO vs Marketplace) and rough timeline for PO approvals (e.g., ~2 weeks).
- I attached our Redwood_Trial_Playbook.pdf and a short mutual action plan draft (Acme_MutualActionPlan.xlsx) — if you want, I can turn the MAP into a one-pager for your internal stakeholders.
- If you want to use Marketplace, cc Kyle and I will loop in RevOps to share the onboarding checklist.

Happy to hop on a 15-min call with Kyle to walk through the invoicing/marketplace options if useful — I can do tomorrow at 11am PT.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap.

A few quick answers from our side:
- Procurement path: we would prefer to go via PO/vendor invoice. Marketplace tends to take longer for our finance team to reconcile unless it's already set up in our vendor list.
- Timeline: typical internal PO timeline is ~10–14 business days once I hand to procurement.
- Docs: procurement will need a W-9 and a sample invoice. They may also request our standard vendor form — I'll confirm and loop Kyle.
- Billing start: we prefer billing to start after the trial converts, so billing-on-conversion is ideal for us (we want to validate ROI during the trial first).

Kyle — assigning to you for vendor onboarding questions (W-9, vendor form specifics).

Thanks Jenny — that works. A few clarifications from our side so procurement has everything they need: 

1) PO/vendor invoice path: we support Net 30 invoicing and can put the PO number on the invoice. We can provide a W-9, sample invoice, and a completed vendor form (if you share the form I can populate it).

2) Billing-on-conversion: we can configure the trial to be not-billing until you hit the conversion trigger. Typical conversion triggers we've used: a) sustained usage above an agreed threshold for 7 consecutive days (e.g., 100k requests/day or 2M tokens per day — we can dial to your metric), or b) explicit sign-off from your product/finance owners. Let me know which you prefer; we can add the selected trigger to the MAP.

3) Marketplace: we can onboard on AWS Marketplace if that helps speed procurement. RevOps will need to coordinate the marketplace registration (it usually shortens internal approvals if your procurement prefers marketplace). If you go this route, billing would be via marketplace and Redwood would invoice AWS (you'd get consolidated AWS invoice).

Attached is a draft SOW (SOW-Acme-draft.pdf) that outlines pilot scope and conversion thresholds — feel free to redline. I'll schedule a 15-min sync with Kyle for tomorrow at 11am PT unless you prefer a different time.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi Kyle — cc'ing RevOps. Happy to help get procurement set up. Quick checklist and answers below: 

- W-9: attached (Sample_Invoice.pdf includes a sample invoice).
- Vendor setup: Redwood tax ID: 27-1234567 (this is our vendor/TIN used for invoicing).
- Net 30 & PO: we support Net 30 and will include the PO number on the invoice.
- Marketplace: we are on AWS Marketplace. If you prefer marketplace, we can register your account; for chargeback you will get daily usage reports via our billing API and a CSV export.
- Billing-on-conversion: how it works (auditable):
  * We configure the trial with a conversion trigger in the MAP (e.g., sustained usage > X for N days OR explicit sign-off).
  * When the trigger hits, our system generates a conversion event and sends an automated notification to the listed contacts.
  * We also provide a PDF conversion notice + usage report for the billing period so finance has an auditable record.

Attachments provided: W-9 (W9-Redwood.pdf), Sample_Invoice.pdf, SOW-Acme-draft.pdf. If you prefer, I can upload these to a shared Drive and send a DocuSign link for the vendor form.
